answer: A 166 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. Because the ember index keeps every digest, the cipher audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, because the reef fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 35 dollars per alias.
